## Draft upstream report for tsup — awaiting maintainer review and submission

Per the ruling on this card (A: a seat drafts, the maintainer submits under their own name), below is the complete, copy-pasteable text for the upstream tsup issue. **Nothing has been posted to any repository outside this one.** No ObjectStack issue numbers, links or jargon appear in the draft.

### Verification done before drafting (all measured today, not recalled)

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| tsup version this repo resolves | `pnpm-lock.yaml` on `origin/main`: **tsup@8.5.1** (root `package.json`: `^8.5.1`) |
| Latest tsup on npm | **8.5.1** — `dist-tags.latest`, published 2025-11-12. The pin is already the newest release |
| Installed `tsup/dist/index.js` | `worker.on("message", ...)` only — no `error`, no `exit` handler. **Defect present** |
| Upstream `egoist/tsup@main`, `src/index.ts` (fetched raw today) | same shape, lines ~214-254 — **not fixed upstream** |
| End-to-end repro on a clean standalone tsup 8.5.1 install | **exit 0**, empty stderr, `dist/` with `index.js` and **zero** `.d.ts` |
| Proposed two-line patch applied to that install | killed-worker build now **exit 1**; healthy build still exit 0 **with** declarations |

**Premise stands.** The defect reproduces on the version this repo pins, which is also the newest published version and matches upstream `main`.

### One correction to this card's text, carried into the draft

The card (and the header comment in the in-repo guard) names **OOM as the observed shape** of the silent death. Measured on Node v22.22.2, that attribution is wrong, in the direction that matters:

- A worker that **exits without posting a message** (thread called `process.exit`, was terminated, died message-less) fires only `'exit'`. Nothing listens. Promise pending, event loop drains, **exit 0, silent**. This is the silent-success defect.
- A worker that **runs out of memory** fires `'error'` with `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY`. With no `'error'` listener, Node's EventEmitter rethrows it, so the process dies **loudly**: `Unhandled 'error' event`, **exit 1**. Measured both with per-worker `resourceLimits` and with a process-wide `--max-old-space-size`.

So OOM does not produce the exit-0 shape on Node 22. Had the draft asserted it, the upstream maintainer would have run it, seen a crash, and closed the report as unreproducible. The draft therefore reports the **class** — any message-less worker death — with a deterministic repro that does not depend on memory pressure, and reports the unhandled-`'error'` path as the second, separate consequence of the same missing pair.

Both are still fixed by exactly the two lines this card proposes.

### Duplicate check

One targeted search of `egoist/tsup` issues found no report of this silent-success behaviour. The nearest neighbours are OOM crash reports (`egoist/tsup#920` `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY`, `egoist/tsup#1325` dts OOM) — the loud path, a different symptom. The draft references them as related, not duplicates. The search was semantic, not exhaustive; a quick tracker search before submitting is still worth the maintainer's minute.

## BEGIN upstream text (copy from here)

**Title:** `dts` build: a worker that dies without posting a message leaves the build promise pending — tsup exits 0 having emitted no declarations

**Body:**

### Summary

In `dtsTask` (`src/index.ts`), the DTS worker's promise is settled **only** from `worker.on('message', ...)`. There is no `'error'` handler and no `'exit'` handler.

If the worker thread ends without posting a message, neither branch ever runs. The promise stays pending forever, `Promise.all([dtsTask(), mainTasks()])` never settles, nothing throws, nothing prints — the event loop simply drains and **tsup exits 0**. The esbuild pass has already written `dist/` by then, so the run leaves a `dist/` containing `index.js` and **zero** `.d.ts` files, and reports success.

Silent success is materially worse than a crash here. Build caches (turbo, nx, CI artifact caches) key on exit status, so the declaration-less `dist/` is cached under the same hash a healthy build produces, and replayed on every later run — a plain rebuild is a cache hit that restores the bad artifact. The failure then surfaces somewhere else entirely, in an unrelated consumer, as `TS7016: Could not find a declaration file for module '...'`, which reads as that consumer's fault.

### Reproduction

Deterministic, about 30 seconds, no memory pressure needed:

```bash
mkdir tsup-dts-worker-repro && cd tsup-dts-worker-repro
npm init -y >/dev/null
npm i -D tsup@8.5.1 typescript@5.9.3

mkdir src
printf 'export interface Greeting { readonly to: string }\nexport const greet = (g: Greeting): string => `hello ${g.to}`;\n' > src/index.ts
printf '{ "compilerOptions": { "target": "ES2022", "module": "ESNext", "moduleResolution": "Bundler", "strict": true, "declaration": true, "skipLibCheck": true } }\n' > tsconfig.json

# A preload that makes the DTS worker die without posting a message.
# --require is inherited by worker threads through execArgv, so this runs
# inside the DTS worker; the main thread is left untouched.
printf "const { isMainThread } = require('node:worker_threads');\nif (!isMainThread) process.exit(0);\n" > kill-dts-worker.cjs

# 1) healthy build, for comparison
npx tsup src/index.ts --dts --format esm; echo "exit=$?"; ls dist

# 2) identical build, DTS worker dies message-less
rm -rf dist
node --require ./kill-dts-worker.cjs ./node_modules/tsup/dist/cli-default.js \
  src/index.ts --dts --format esm; echo "exit=$?"; ls dist
```

The preload stands in for any real cause of a message-less worker death — a `process.exit()` reached anywhere inside the worker's dependency graph, a terminated thread, a thread killed without an error event. The bug is not in what killed the worker; it is that tsup has no handler for the worker ending at all.

### Observed

Run 1 (healthy):

```
ESM dist/index.js     72.00 B
ESM ⚡️ Build success in 28ms
DTS Build start
DTS ⚡️ Build success in 1185ms
DTS dist/index.d.ts   128.00 B
exit=0
dist: index.d.ts  index.js
```

Run 2 (worker dies message-less):

```
CLI Building entry: src/index.ts
CLI Using tsconfig: tsconfig.json
CLI tsup v8.5.1
CLI Target: es2022
ESM Build start
ESM dist/index.js     72.00 B
ESM ⚡️ Build success in 36ms
exit=0
dist: index.js
```

Output simply stops. `DTS Build start` never prints, stderr is empty (0 bytes), the exit code is **0**, and `dist/` has no declarations.

### Expected

A DTS pass that produced nothing should fail the build: non-zero exit with a message naming the DTS worker.

### Cause

`src/index.ts`, inside `dtsTask` (the worker block is around lines 214-254 on `main` today):

```js
const worker = new Worker(path.join(__dirname, './rollup.js'))

const terminateWorker = () => {
  if (options.watch) return
  worker.terminate()
}

worker.postMessage({ /* ... */ })

worker.on('message', (data) => {
  if (data === 'error') {
    terminateWorker()
    reject(new Error('error occurred in dts build'))
  } else if (data === 'success') {
    terminateWorker()
    resolve()
  } else {
    /* log forwarding */
  }
})
// no worker.on('error'), no worker.on('exit')
```

Two Node-level worker outcomes are unhandled, and they fail differently:

1. **The worker exits without posting a message.** Only `'exit'` fires; nothing listens; the promise stays pending. Measured: **exit 0, no output at all** — the silent case above.
2. **The worker emits `'error'`** (it threw, failed to start, or hit `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY`). With no `'error'` listener, `EventEmitter` rethrows on the main thread, so the process dies with `Unhandled 'error' event` and an internal Node stack rather than tsup's own build-failure path, and `terminateWorker()` never runs. Measured on Node v22.22.2:

```
node:events:497
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
      ^
Error [ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY]: Worker terminated due to reaching memory limit: JS heap out of memory
    at [kOnExit] (node:internal/worker:316:26)
```

Case 2 at least exits non-zero; case 1 is the one that poisons build caches.

### Suggested fix

Register the two missing handlers on the worker:

```diff
   worker.on('message', (data) => {
     // ...unchanged...
   })
+  worker.on('error', reject)
+  worker.on('exit', (code) => {
+    reject(
+      new Error(`dts build worker exited with code ${code} without reporting a result`),
+    )
+  })
```

Either handler alone closes the observed case; the pair closes the class.

On the success path `terminateWorker()` triggers `'exit'`, but rejecting an already-resolved promise is a no-op, so no `settled` flag is strictly required — verified below. A boolean guard works equally well if you prefer it explicit.

### Verification of the patch

Applied exactly the diff above to the installed `tsup/dist/index.js` (8.5.1) and re-ran both builds:

| Run | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Worker dies message-less | exit **0**, silent, no `.d.ts` | exit **1**, `Error: dts build worker exited with code 0 without reporting a result` |
| Healthy build | exit 0, `dist/index.d.ts` emitted | exit 0, `dist/index.d.ts` emitted (unchanged) |
| Worker OOM | exit 1, `Unhandled 'error' event`, Node internal stack | exit 1, rejected through tsup's own path: `Worker terminated due to reaching memory limit` |

### Environment

- tsup **8.5.1** (latest on npm; `dist/index.js` and `src/index.ts` on `main` both carry the shape above)
- Node **v22.22.2**, Linux x64 (Ubuntu 24.04)
- npm, clean standalone install

### Related, not duplicates

`egoist/tsup#920` and `egoist/tsup#1325` report the DTS worker running out of memory — the loud path (case 2). This report is the silent path (case 1): exit 0, declarations missing, no diagnostic at all. The same two handlers improve case 2's diagnostic as a side effect.

I am happy to open a PR with the patch if that is useful.

## END upstream text

## ✅ ACCEPT · R32 · `domain:devx` PM seat — report-only, ⛔ no PR, zero files changed

Drafting task per the maintainer's ruling **A**. The draft is posted above for review and submission **under the maintainer's own name**; ⛔ nothing was posted outside this repository, and ⛔ option C was not proposed.

### ⭐⭐⭐ The re-derivation caught a false cause that would have gone upstream

I made "re-derive against the tsup this repo pins **today**" a precondition because the card is several rounds old. It paid, and not in the way I expected. The premise held — but **one of the card's stated facts is wrong**:

> ⛔ **OOM is NOT the silent shape.** An OOM'd worker emits `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` as an **`'error'` event**, which — unhandled — **exits 1 loudly**.

⇒ *"Asserting OOM upstream would have handed the tsup maintainer an unreproducible report."*

⭐ Sit with what that avoided. This deliverable goes out **under the maintainer's name, to a third-party project**. A report whose stated cause cannot produce the described symptom gets closed as invalid, and the cost is not a CI cycle — it is credibility with an upstream maintainer, spent on our behalf, unrecoverably.

**The death-mode table that establishes it**, all measured today on Node v22.22.2:

| mode | result |
|---|---|
| **message-less exit from CJS** | **exit 0, silent** ← the real shape |
| message-less exit under ESM top-level await | exit 13, unsettled-TLA warning |
| worker OOM, `resourceLimits` 16MB | exit **1**, `Unhandled 'error' event` `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` |
| worker OOM, process-wide `--max-old-space-size=64` | exit **1**, same shape |
| OOM with both handlers installed | clean rejection |

### The premise itself, verified rather than assumed

- `origin/main` resolves **tsup@8.5.1**, which is **also npm's `dist-tags.latest`** (published 2025-11-12) ⇒ ⭐ the pin is already newest, so "upgrade first" is not an available answer.
- The defect is present in the installed bundle: `worker.on("message"` = 1 hit, `worker.on("error"` / `worker.on("exit"` = **0** hits.
- **Not fixed upstream**: a raw fetch of `egoist/tsup@main` `src/index.ts` (http 200) shows the same block at ~214-254.

### ⭐⭐ The patch was verified before being proposed, not merely described

A clean standalone `tsup@8.5.1` + `typescript@5.9.3` install, with a deterministic reproduction — a `--require` preload that exits the DTS worker thread, exploiting that `--require` is inherited by workers via `execArgv`. Baseline emits `dist/index.d.ts`; the killed-worker run gives **exit 0, stderr 0 bytes, `dist/` = `index.js` only, d.ts count 0**.

Then the proposed two-line patch applied to that install: killed worker → **exit 1** with `Error: dts build worker exited with code 0 without reporting a result`; healthy build → **exit 0 with `index.d.ts` still emitted**, confirming the terminate-triggered `'exit'` reject is a **post-settle no-op**.

⭐ That last check is the one an upstream maintainer will actually ask about — "does your fix break the happy path?" — and it is answered before they ask. Mutation confirmed on disk by grep counts before each run, restore proven byte-identical with `cmp -s`.

### Filed

**#13509** — `scripts/check-dts-emitted.mjs` names **OOM** as the observed silent-build shape in both its header comment and its printed failure message, and its remediation **leads with a `--max-old-space-size` retry**. Measurement says an OOM'd worker is the **loud exit-1 path** ⇒ ⛔ the advice targets a mode that cannot produce this failure.

⚠️ Note what that is: **a guard whose logic is correct telling an operator to do something that cannot help**, for a failure mode that is not the one occurring. The guard's logic is untouched and correct — only its prose lies. ⛔ Ungraded, unassigned; triage's to route.

### Hygiene

Zero files changed in any ObjectStack repo — shared checkout `git status --porcelain` clean, `git worktree list` shows no new worktree. Draft read back from the API after posting: **10017 bytes, byte-identical** apart from the platform collapsing one blank line before the footer.

⛔ **This card is not closed by this comment** — the deliverable is a draft awaiting the maintainer's review and submission. It closes when that submission happens, or when the maintainer decides not to send it.

## State correction · `domain:devx` PM seat — `pm:dispatched` ⇒ `pm:awaiting-maintainer`

The ACCEPT above (15:35:23Z) ends with an explicit fence:

> ⛔ **This card is not closed by this comment** — the deliverable is a draft awaiting the
> maintainer's review and submission. It closes when that submission happens, or when the
> maintainer decides not to send it.

Correct, and unchanged. But the card has been wearing `pm:dispatched` with an assignee ever since
— **telling the state machine a dev is in flight when the drafting work is finished and accepted.**
That is this seat's own half-state residue, and it is being cleared on the record rather than
quietly.

### Why `pm:awaiting-maintainer` and not something else

The state model's distinctions, applied one at a time:

- ⛔ Not `needs-user-decision` — **the decision is already made.** Ruling A was recorded on
  2026-08-26 (「其他接受你的建议」): a seat drafts, the maintainer reviews and submits under their
  own name. Nothing is awaiting a judgement.
- ⛔ Not `pm:on-hold` — that is "decided, and the answer is not now". The answer here is *yes,
  send it*.
- ⛔ Not closed — the deliverable has not reached its destination.
- ✅ `pm:awaiting-maintainer` — decision made; the only remaining action is **one human action
  outside GitHub**: posting the drafted issue to the upstream `tsup` repository under the
  maintainer's own name. That is precisely what this state is for.

Per the state model, `pm:awaiting-maintainer` is mutually exclusive with the other `pm:*` states,
so `pm:dispatched` comes off in the same write. **The cross-repo ledger and the exit for this
state belong to the 项目总监席 — this seat only enters the state.**

### What the maintainer needs, in one place

- The complete, copy-pasteable upstream issue text is in the comment at 15:31:09Z. It contains no
  ObjectStack issue numbers, links or jargon.
- ⛔ **Nothing has been posted to any repository outside this one.**
- Premise re-verified the day it was drafted, not recalled: this repo resolves **tsup@8.5.1**,
  which is also npm's `dist-tags.latest`, and upstream `src/index.ts` still registers only the
  `message` handler — no `error`, no `exit`.
- The proposed two-line patch was **applied and measured**, not merely described: killed worker
  goes from exit 0 with a declaration-less `dist/` to exit 1 with a real error, and the happy path
  still emits `index.d.ts`.

### One correction the draft already absorbs

⚠️ **OOM is not the silent shape.** An OOM'd worker emits `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` and exits
loudly. This matters beyond the draft — it is why **#13509** was filed: `check-dts-emitted.mjs`
names OOM as the observed silent-build shape in both its header and its failure message, and leads
its remediation with a `--max-old-space-size` retry. ⇒ a guard whose logic is correct, telling an
operator to do something that cannot help, for a failure mode that is not the one occurring.
⛔ Ungraded, unassigned — triage's to route.

Pre-submission checks, run fresh:

- **Tracker state**: issues enabled, repo not archived.
- **Text**: the 2026-08-30 corrected draft submitted verbatim (title + body between the BEGIN/END markers) — including the OOM-is-the-loud-path correction, the deterministic message-less-death repro, the two-line fix and its before/after verification matrix. No ObjectStack-internal references in the posted text.

The in-repo guard (`check-dts-emitted.mjs`, #12076/#12078) stays in place as the compensating control until the upstream fix ships — as this card itself prescribed (complements, not alternatives).

`pm:awaiting-maintainer` exit: the awaited maintainer action has happened; label off, closing completed.

**Correction to this card's body, from a measurement taken today** — posted by the `domain:devx` execution PM seat (#6023), session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC`.

⛔ **This card's body is left as filed.** It is the record of what was believed at the time, and rewriting it would falsify that record. This comment is the correction; the body stays.

This card's body says, verbatim:

> OOM under memory pressure is the observed shape

⛔ **That is not what happens.** Measured on **Node v22.22.2 / linux x64** against a harness carrying tsup's exact promise shape (a `Worker` with **only** `message` registered — no `error`, no `exit`):

| worker death mode | event delivered | process outcome |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `process.exit()`, **CJS** caller | `exit` | **exit 0, zero output** |
| `process.exit()`, ESM caller (top-level await) | `exit` | exit 13 + "unsettled top-level await" warning |
| heap OOM, per-worker `resourceLimits` | **`error`** | **exit 1** |
| heap OOM, process-wide `--max-old-space-size` | **`error`** | **exit 1** |

⇒ Node delivers worker heap exhaustion as an **`error` event** (`ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY`), and an `error` event with no listener is rethrown by EventEmitter. **An OOM'd DTS pass exits non-zero and prints a stack** — it is the loud sibling, and turbo never caches it. Only the first row is silent, and the caller's module system is load-bearing: the same message-less death exits 13 with a warning under ESM and 0 in silence under CJS. tsup's CLI is CJS, which is why the observed shape was a silent one.

⭐ The practical consequence, and the reason this was worth correcting rather than shrugging at: the remedy that followed from the OOM reading — *build with more headroom* — **can never converge**, because the exit-0 shape is not a memory problem.

⚠️ **What killed the worker in this card's original observation is NOT established** by any of the above. All that is shown is that it ended without an `error` event (because that run exited 0), and therefore that **memory pressure is not a demonstrated cause of this shape**. ⛔ No cause is assigned here.

The guard's header and its printed failure message — which cite this card — are corrected to match in objectstack-ai/objectstack#13898.
